sources.note: Nothing on stress; unsourced continuum-level claims (9-vowel ATR system; 'three tones.. mid, low and high') citing only Ethnologue and Blackings & Fabb's Ma'di grammar (a different family). Not a description of Nyamusa.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page nyam1279 (refs: Evans-Pritchard 1937; Campbell et al. 2022 ELCat; Glottolog's most extensive descriptions Persson 1997 and Evans-Pritchard 1937, both 'a wordlist or less'; dialects Nyamusa [nyam1280], Molo [molo1259]; sister of Jur Modo under 'Lori' [lori1239])
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; bibliographic record only. Confirms no grammar, sketch or phonology of Nyamusa-Molo exists (both Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are wordlist-level).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)

sources.citation: Persson, Janet. 2004. Bongo-Bagirmi languages in Sudan. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 77-84. Entebbe: SIL-Sudan.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for any language. Only Nyamusa sentence (p. 77): 'To the west of the Modo live the Nyamusa, whose language is close to Jur Modo.' Points to Persson 1997 OPSL 7 for the comparative survey and to a 1978 SIL/IRL survey of the 'Jur' dialects. The phonology sketch (pp. 79-80) is of Jur Modo only.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. 1934. Survey of the language groups in the Southern Sudan. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 7: 861-896.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; distribution only: 'The Nyamusa (600 taxpayers) live north of the Wira, also under Chief Dokolo, but their language is not so closely allied'; 'Lori and Lali are much more like Nyamusa and the so-called Moru dialects.'

sources.citation: archive.org-wide full-text probes ('Nyamusa'; 'Nyamusa' stress; 'Nyamusa-Molo'; 122/83/16 hits) and SIL OAI-OLAC harvest (~53k records, held)
sources.note: No description of the language anywhere: hits are ethnographic (Seligman 1932, Baxter & Butt 1953, Evans-Pritchard introductions), classificatory (Homburger 1949, Murdock, Int. Encyc. of Linguistics, Ethnologue editions) or unrelated. SIL OAI harvest: 0 records for nwm/Nyamusa.

sources.citation: Persson, Andrew M. 1997. Grouping of the Bongo-Baka languages. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 7: 19-39. Nairobi: SIL-Sudan.

sources.note: Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for nyam1279 and the only linguistic publication with Nyamusa data (comparative wordlists of the Baka-Morokodo-Jur Modo-Nyamusa-'Beli chain; may carry tone/accent marking or prosodic notes).

sources.note: Nearest relative with a first-hand stress statement (Jur Modo, 70-75% lexically similar; sec. 2e Stress p. 49: penultimate with exceptions). Already held under jurm1239; listed only as the comparative anchor, NOT as a Nyamusa source.

sources.citation: SIL-Sudan / Institute of Regional Languages. 1978. Survey of the 'Jur' dialects (unpublished; named in Persson 2004 OPSL 9 p. 78). Any SIL South Sudan wordlist or survey report for Nyamusa-Molo [nwm].

sources.note: The only field data on Nyamusa beyond Persson 1997; a transcribed wordlist with accent/tone marks would be the first primary evidence. Not in the SIL OAI-OLAC feed; enquiry to SIL South Sudan needed.
